content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent API structure, DTO names, and validation rules. This skill applies Allra Spring Boot conventions for packages, REST endpoints, and response objects.
actual_capabilities: Recommend a domain package structure for Spring Boot backend code.
Define request, response, and internal DTO naming conventions.
Guide record-based DTO creation with Bean Validation annotations.
Outline REST controller route and HTTP method conventions.
Describe standard success and error response shapes.
Provide a checklist for reviewing new API endpoints.
limitations: It does not inspect a running service or verify compiled code.
Project-specific package names and versioning rules may need adjustment.
It does not design database schemas or persistence behavior.
It does not replace security, privacy, or production readiness review.

use_cases.title: Create a new domain API
use_cases.description: Plan package layout, DTO names, controller routes, and validation before implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize DTO conventions
use_cases.description: Align request, response, and internal DTO names across a Spring Boot service.

use_cases.title: Review API consistency
use_cases.description: Compare new endpoints against Allra package, REST, and response conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Spring Boot endpoint for creating a customer. Follow the Allra package structure, DTO naming, and validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Build DTO conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Define request, response, and internal DTO names for an order domain. Explain where each DTO belongs in the package structure.

prompt_templates.title: Review controller design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned REST controller against Allra API rules. Check routes, methods, request validation, and response consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full domain API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a domain API plan for invoices with package layout, controller responsibilities, DTO records, validation fields, and success and error responses.

output_examples.input: User asks for a new product creation API.
output: Recommended domain package layout for the product feature.
Request, response, and internal DTO names with clear responsibilities.
Controller route, validation, and response consistency checklist.

output_examples.input: User asks whether DTO names are consistent.
output_examples.output: A review that separates client request, client response, and internal transfer DTOs, with naming corrections and rationale.

output_examples.input: User asks for response format guidance.
output_examples.output: A concise recommendation for success and error response shapes, with notes about keeping project-wide consistency.

best_practices: Keep domain packages grouped by API, DTO, entity, repository, and service responsibilities.
Use records for simple DTOs and Bean Validation for request payloads.
Apply one response format consistently across related endpoints.
anti_patterns: Mixing request, response, and internal DTOs without clear package boundaries.
Using entity objects directly as client API payloads.
Changing API versioning style without checking project policy.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.2 projects that use common backend patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate complete production code?
faq.answer: It guides structure and examples. The user or agent must still implement business logic and tests.

faq.question: Can it be used outside Allra projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but package names, response formats, and versioning should be adapted to the local project.

faq.question: Does it cover validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Bean Validation annotations for request DTOs.

faq.question: Does it define database schema rules?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on API design, DTO naming, package structure, and controller conventions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
